author: WP16
summary: Alpha.1-era overview of sharp-runtime as a project in its own right: scale, include roots, the opt-in Object, String/Exception adaptation, EventHandler/MulticastAction, TimeSpan and fail-fast collections, the Task model, permanent scope boundaries, the modular build and CI scope. Every count is stale at sharp-runtime next @ 41b918c9 (1,097 headers, 44 modules/47 names, 81 CNA includes, three Object subclasses, ten CI configurations) and the serialization boundary narrowed. libcna.com had only the ecosystem summary, the build seam and Tutorial 89; the runtime semantics now live on four new sharp-runtime deep dives.

concepts.section: Why sharp-runtime Exists
concepts.text: sharp-runtime is a project in its own right: a C++23 practical subset of .NET System.* that deliberately implements no CLR, JIT or garbage collector, much wider in scope than the XNA vocabulary CNA needs.

concepts.section: Scale
concepts.text: Size of sharp-runtime at 41b918c9: 1,097 public headers (1,090 System/, 7 SharpRuntime/), 9 private headers and 230 implementation files (the older 1,032/5/217 figures are stale).
concepts.note: Bible counts 1,032/5/217 were for the 2026-08-10 tree.

concepts.section: Scale
concepts.text: Test code versus production code depends on the counting method: by physical lines at 41b918c9 tests are 187,414 lines and production 191,545; the older ~30 % excess came from a code-line counter on an older tree.

target.evidence: sharp-runtime@41b918c9:git grep -c "" over modules/*/include, src, tests and tests/

concepts.section: Scale
concepts.text: The recorded GoogleTest state is not all-green and moves: NEXT.md records 17,934 tests across 39 executables on 2026-08-31 and, on 2026-09-19, five Xml.Linq failures; a static count gives 17,432 definitions.

concepts.section: Scale
concepts.text: The surface extends to System.Text.Json, XML LINQ and XPath, buffers, channels, WebSockets and HTTP, far beyond a minimal XNA-support subset; CNA links only a small part.

concepts.section: Namespace structure
concepts.text: Public headers live below exactly two include roots: System/ mirrors the .NET namespace tree and SharpRuntime/ holds project helpers that are not part of the .NET mirror.
tokens: Two include roots and the transliteration rule

concepts.section: Namespace structure
concepts.text: System/ carries the nested .NET namespaces (Collections.Concurrent/Frozen/Generic/Immutable/ObjectModel/Specialized, IO.Compression/Hashing/IsolatedStorage, Net.*, Text.*, Threading.*) plus 225 flat top-level type headers.

concepts.section: Namespace structure
concepts.text: SharpRuntime/SharpRuntimeHelper.hpp holds the primitive alias table (bytecs, intcs, Single and the rest) that CNA's public surface uses.

concepts.section: Namespace structure
concepts.text: There is no umbrella header; the include spelling is a mechanical transliteration of the fully qualified .NET name (System.IO.FileStream -> System/IO/FileStream.hpp).

concepts.section: Namespace structure
concepts.text: CNA's production sources include 81 distinct sharp-runtime headers (78 System/, 3 SharpRuntime/: SharpRuntimeHelper.hpp, Prop.hpp, Storage/StoragePaths.hpp), not two.

concepts.section: Namespace structure
concepts.text: Prop.hpp exports property-declaration macros used downstream; inside sharp-runtime only the two Experimental property headers include it, CNA uses it in public headers.
concepts.note: Bible said no runtime module includes it.

concepts.section: Object and IDisposable: deliberately not two roots
concepts.text: System::Object is an abstract, opt-in compatibility type (pure virtual GetTypeName); only DateTime, DateTimeOffset and System::Timers::Timer derive from it in sharp-runtime.

concepts.section: Object and IDisposable: deliberately not two roots
concepts.text: Stream does not derive from Object and exceptions derive from std::exception, so importing .NET's universal-root invariant into the C++ types is wrong.

concepts.section: Object and IDisposable: deliberately not two roots
concepts.text: GetTypeNameHPP()/GetTypeNameCPP() only reduce override boilerplate; they are not evidence that every ported class inherits Object.

concepts.section: Object and IDisposable: deliberately not two roots
concepts.text: System::IDisposable is one pure virtual Dispose(); C++ has no using, so callers use RAII or call Dispose() explicitly, implementations must be idempotent; it is a capability interface, not a second root.
tokens: safe to call more than once

concepts.section: String and Exception expose the same adaptation strategy
concepts.text: System::String is a non-instantiable static helper class (constructor and destructor deleted); runtime strings stay std::string, also exported as SharpRuntime::String.

concepts.section: String and Exception expose the same adaptation strategy
concepts.text: System::Exception derives from std::exception, keeps its inner exception as std::exception_ptr, defaults HResult to 0x80131500 and returns an empty stack trace.

concepts.section: EventHandler and MulticastAction: solving a problem C# doesn't have
concepts.text: EventHandler<T> must be both the delegate type and the subscriber list because C++ has no event keyword: operator+=, token Add/Remove, Clear() and Raise(sender, e).

concepts.section: EventHandler and MulticastAction: solving a problem C# doesn't have
concepts.text: Raise invokes over a snapshot of the handler list so a handler removing itself mid-raise cannot destroy the running std::function, which previously escaped as std::bad_function_call.

concepts.section: EventHandler and MulticastAction: solving a problem C# doesn't have
concepts.text: SetReplayHook() replays existing state to each new subscriber; CNA's NetworkSession sets it on GamerJoined so subscribing reports gamers already in the session.

concepts.section: EventHandler and MulticastAction: solving a problem C# doesn't have
concepts.text: MulticastAction<Args...> is a purpose-built multicast field with token removal and snapshot invocation, because std::function has no target-plus-method equality for -=.

concepts.section: EventHandler and MulticastAction: solving a problem C# doesn't have
concepts.text: MulticastAction's motivating case, named in its header, is re-parenting a transform hierarchy (cna-extended) where one specific subscription must be dropped without clearing the others.
tokens: re-parenting a transform hierarchy in cna-extended
concepts.note: The header attributes the case to cna-extended, not to CNA itself.

concepts.section: Value types used by later chapters
concepts.text: TimeSpan stores 100-nanosecond ticks and underlies CNA's GameTime, TargetElapsedTime and sensor update intervals.

concepts.section: Value types used by later chapters
concepts.text: TimeSpan's static copy/move counters are std::atomic<int> with relaxed ordering since 9c2cb0ae (2026-07-07); CNA's devices-tsan preset text that reports a TimeSpan race describes an older sharp-runtime.

concepts.section: Value types used by later chapters
concepts.text: List and Dictionary implement .NET's fail-fast rule: a mutation while an enumerator is open makes the next step throw InvalidOperationException.

concepts.section: Value types used by later chapters
concepts.text: Dictionary::Remove bumps the version although .NET's does not, because erasing the std::unordered_map element an iterator points at invalidates it; Clear bumps too.

concepts.section: Value types used by later chapters
concepts.text: The fail-fast invariant is project-wide: every mutable collection uses the shared MutationCounter class (plus SortedSet's single tree version).
concepts.note: Now one shared type rather than per-collection counters.

concepts.section: Value types used by later chapters
concepts.text: OrderedDictionary::EnsureCapacity needed its own fix: it now bumps the version only when capacity grows, as .NET does; before, an enumerator across a reallocation went undetected.

concepts.section: Concurrency primitives
concepts.text: Task::Wait() rethrows a faulted task's stored exception directly, without AggregateException, and throws TaskCanceledException for a canceled task.
tokens: rethrows a faulted task's stored exception directly

concepts.section: Concurrency primitives
concepts.text: ContinueWith captures the antecedent state through a weak pointer so the continuation chain cannot keep itself alive, and no extra thread is spawned per continuation.

concepts.section: Concurrency primitives
concepts.text: There is no thread pool or scheduler: continuations run inline on the completing thread or immediately on the caller, as if ExecuteSynchronously were always set; Task::Run itself uses one std::async thread per task.
concepts.note: Added that tasks themselves are one thread each and throw PlatformNotSupportedException on single-threaded Emscripten.

concepts.section: Concurrency primitives
concepts.text: NotOnFaulted/NotOnCanceled/NotOnRanToCompletion (and OnlyOn compositions) are honoured; PreferFairness, LongRunning, AttachedToParent, DenyChildAttach, HideScheduler and LazyCancellation are accepted for API parity only.

concepts.section: WhenAll cancellation and the external-future bridge
concepts.text: WhenAny registers an inline callback per input; the first to win an atomic compare-exchange completes the result, so no watcher thread is created (rebuilt 2026-07-14).

concepts.section: WhenAll cancellation and the external-future bridge
concepts.text: WhenAll waits for every input without short-circuiting and rethrows the first fault in input order instead of an AggregateException.

concepts.section: WhenAll cancellation and the external-future bridge
concepts.text: If no input faulted but one was canceled, waiting on WhenAll throws TaskCanceledException while the returned task's status reads Faulted: a documented deviation.

concepts.section: WhenAll cancellation and the external-future bridge
concepts.text: WhenAll classifies cancellation by the input's status, not by exception type; TaskCompletionSource uses a separate producer-set atomic flag so SetException(TaskCanceledException) stays Faulted.

concepts.section: WhenAll cancellation and the external-future bridge
concepts.text: WhenAny's outer TaskT<Task> always completes successfully with the first terminal input; the caller inspects that task's status.

concepts.section: Concurrency primitives
concepts.text: Threading::Thread wraps std::thread, does not start at construction, and a second Start() throws ThreadStateException (.NET's one-shot contract).

concepts.section: Permanent scope boundaries: what will never be ported, and why
concepts.text: The project's rules list "known permanent deviations (not bugs, not TODO)"; at 41b918c9 the list is longer than five areas.
concepts.note: Adds the UTF-8 unit, normalization and tzdata deviations.

concepts.section: Permanent scope boundaries: what will never be ported, and why
concepts.text: Reflection (Type, Activator, Enum.GetNames/GetValues) is completely out of scope and stubs are the correct end state.
tokens: Stubs are the correct end state

concepts.section: Permanent scope boundaries: what will never be ported, and why
concepts.text: GC mutating calls are no-ops and queries return fixed sentinels (zero, false, NotApplicable, MaxGeneration 2); memory is RAII and shared_ptr.

concepts.section: Permanent scope boundaries: what will never be ported, and why
concepts.text: Serialization has no serializer, but since 2026-09-20 SerializationInfo is a real name-to-value store so CNA's exceptions can keep XNA's serialization constructor signature.

concepts.section: Permanent scope boundaries: what will never be ported, and why
concepts.text: P/Invoke and native interop are out of scope.

concepts.section: Permanent scope boundaries: what will never be ported, and why
concepts.text: Encryption, X.509 and TLS are out of scope by a 2026-07-07 decision while MD5/SHA*/HMAC/PBKDF2 stay ported; HMAC keys and PBKDF2 passwords are still secret material.
tokens: HMAC keys and PBKDF2 passwords are still secret material

concepts.section: Reflection's stub and its deliberate contradiction
concepts.text: Type::From<T>() is RTTI-backed; its IsClass/IsValueType/... predicates return fixed values that are not mutually consistent (From<int>() is a class and not a value type), so code must not branch on them.

concepts.section: Reflection's stub and its deliberate contradiction
concepts.text: Activator keeps compile-time construction (CreateInstance<T>(), a variadic CreateInstance<T>(args...), CreateInstancePtr) and has no overload taking a runtime Type or CreateInstanceFrom.
concepts.note: Bible: only CreateInstance<T>(); a variadic forwarding form now exists (#2266).

concepts.section: The build is part of the public architecture
concepts.text: Since the 2026-08-10 modularisation sharp-runtime is not one archive; at 41b918c9 44 module directories register 47 names: 33 static, 13 interface, 1 alias.

concepts.section: The build is part of the public architecture
concepts.text: Core and Collections are compatibility umbrellas coexisting with narrower components.

concepts.section: The build is part of the public architecture
concepts.text: An include path names a source-level dependency while a SharpRuntime::<Component> target declares the link closure.

concepts.section: The build is part of the public architecture
concepts.text: On Android the Storage component links SDL3 privately only if an SDL3 target already exists (StoragePaths calls SDL_GetAndroidInternalStoragePath), so CNA creates SDL first; it is not a general SDL dependency.

concepts.section: Local and tracked CI gates have different scope
concepts.text: The local gate (scripts/local_ci_check.sh) builds the production graph with Clang -Werror and then the full GCC build and tests under fail-fast shell handling.

concepts.section: Local and tracked CI gates have different scope
concepts.text: The modular test topology is one executable per component that owns tests plus one integration executable; at 41b918c9 40 of 44 module directories own tests.
tokens: 40 of the 44 module directories own tests

concepts.section: Local and tracked CI gates have different scope
concepts.text: Each component test links only its component and declared test-only dependencies, so an undeclared cross-module use fails at link time instead of hiding in a monolith.

concepts.section: Local and tracked CI gates have different scope
concepts.text: Python meta-tests and deliberately failing consumer fixtures add build-boundary checks that positive unit tests cannot express.

concepts.section: Local and tracked CI gates have different scope
concepts.text: components.yml runs on push and pull request: ten selective component configurations, a full compatibility job and a Doxygen-warning job, with SHARP_RUNTIME_BUILD_JOBS 2, all on Ubuntu.

concepts.section: Local and tracked CI gates have different scope
concepts.text: Workflow presence proves a hosted trigger and named Linux jobs, not Windows, macOS or Emscripten execution or that every historical commit passed.
tokens: supplies no Windows, macOS or Emscripten execution

concepts.section: Recorded failures and platform claims need scope
concepts.text: Recorded failures stay in the record; an older baseline claiming every test passes describes a different revision.
tokens: older claims that every test passes
concepts.note: At 41b918c9 the last entry records five Xml.Linq failures rather than six unrelated ones.

concepts.section: Recorded failures and platform claims need scope
concepts.text: A native Linux pass, a MinGW or Emscripten cross-compile of the libraries and execution of cross-built tests are three separate results; the README records only compile scope for MinGW and Emscripten.
